g.title: p_ot
g.text: talos-ottawa
— the hub
Runs the singletons the other two borrow:
Mimir, VictoriaLogs, Grafana, Tinyauth, the Zot
registry and the Open Cluster Management hub.
Rook-Ceph · SMB · Garage pools

g.title: p_rb
g.text: talos-robbinsdale
home automation and media
Rook-Ceph · SMB · Garage pools
Borrows Ottawa's telemetry stack and Tinyauth.

g.title: t_op
g.text: tailscale-operator
— one per cluster
Creates every device below from ProxyClass
templates. Its OAuth credentials are
SOPS-encrypted like everything else.

g.title: p_ot->t_op
g.text: LOCATION=ottawa

g.title: s_ceph
g.text: Rook-Ceph
— Ottawa and Robbinsdale only
Block and filesystem, one CephCluster each, both
on v20 — which IS Tentacle. Nothing is held back a
major version; what is bounded is an mgr logging
bug that floods the recent-log ring, capped by
log_max_recent 100 until the fix lands (rook#17786).
There is no CephObjectStore anywhere: all object
storage is Garage.

g.title: p_sp
g.text: talos-stpetersburg
AI inference on two DGX Spark GB10 machines
No Ceph at all — local-path for every tier,
plus its own Garage pools.

g.title: s_bulk
g.text: Bulk and node-local
csi-driver-smb — media libraries, never databases
local-path — every St. Petersburg tier, the model
weights, and the backing store under the Garage
hostPath pools

g.title: p_sp->s_bulk
g.text: no Ceph here

g.title: t_policy
g.text: tailscale/policy.hujson
One central zero-trust policy: groups, tags,
per-location ipsets, autoApprovers, recorded SSH,
and grants that permit location-to-location
traffic only through that location's own subnet
router. Its tests run in CI beside it.

g.title: t_policy->t_op
g.text: authorises every
device the operator makes

g.title: t_router
g.text: Subnet router and app connector
advertise the LAN, pod, service and LoadBalancer
CIDRs, plus a per-site 4via6 /96 range

g.title: t_api
g.text: kube-apiserver ProxyGroup
serves <location>-k8s-operator.keiretsu.ts.net
TAILNET IDENTITY IS THE CREDENTIAL, which is why
the committed kubeconfig carries no client cert,
no key and only a placeholder token.

g.title: t_egress
g.text: Egress ProxyGroup common-egress
Backs every tailnet-fqdn Service, and therefore
every cross-cluster dependency on this page.

g.title: t_dns
g.text: DNSConfig ts-dns
A LoadBalancer nameserver that CoreDNS forwards
ts.net to, so that pods — not just laptops — can
resolve tailnet names.

g.title: t_contract
g.text: The pod-side egress contract
THE RULE THAT KEEPS BREAKING PEOPLE.
For every tailnet name a pod consumes, declare in
that namespace an ExternalName Service annotated
with the tailnet FQDN and proxy-group:
common-egress. The operator rewrites it to a proxy
address and ts-dns republishes the original name.
ts-dns PUBLISHES ONLY NAMES AN EGRESS SERVICE
DECLARES — not every MagicDNS device.
Verify TailscaleEgressSvcReady=True AND resolve
the name from a throwaway pod. A laptop dig proves
nothing: laptops use MagicDNS, pods do not.
Never publish tailnet CGNAT addresses in public DNS.

g.title: t_dns->t_contract
g.text: publishes only what
egress declares

g.title: s_garage
g.text: Garage — one logical S3 estate, three zones
Every cluster runs a GarageCluster, and each one
lists all three zones and reaches the others over
the tailnet. Replication factor 3, consistency
mode degraded.

g.title: s_gw
g.text: Apps never address the storage tier
They use ${COMMON_S3_ENDPOINT}, the cluster-local
gateway, for two reasons: the gateway carries the
full key table so an S3 signature resolves
locally, and it survives local storage loss by
proxying reads to a surviving zone.

g.title: s_garage->s_gw
g.text: every app enters here

g.title: s_pools
g.text: Garage local pools
hostPath-backed and declared per node. The storage
tier is Manual at all three sites, deliberately, so
an array can be moved between backing stores; the
gateway tier stays operator-managed.

g.title: s_garage->s_pools
g.text: Manual storage tier

g.title: s_buckets
g.text: Buckets
velero · mimir · zot · tailscale-logs, plus one
<db>-postgres bucket per database so that
federated sites never share a Barman catalog.
Per-app credentials are minted by GarageKey CRs.

g.title: s_rpc
g.text: Why Garage needs so many egress Services
Its RPC is identity-authenticated per node, so it
needs one ingress identity and one egress Service
PER REMOTE NODE. A single shared L4 VIP cannot
route a node identifier, so the usual one-Service
shortcut does not work here.

g.title: s_rpc->t_egress
g.text: one egress Service
per remote node

g.title: s_db
g.text: Databases, caches and backup
CloudNativePG — 10 Postgres clusters, streaming
WAL and base backups to Garage
Dragonfly — every cache; there is no real Redis in
this repository, whatever the filenames say
Velero — kopia file backup, not CSI snapshots

g.title: s_db->s_garage
g.text: WAL, base backups
and Velero archives

g.title: o_local
g.text: In every cluster
kube-prometheus-stack · Fluent Bit · Gatus
Kromgo · blackbox and host exporters.
Prometheus stamps externalLabels cluster=<name>,
which is what keeps the three sites' series apart
once they all land in one Mimir.
Fluent Bit also receives Talos KERNEL logs over
TCP, because every machine ships them there.

g.title: o_store
g.text: Ottawa only
Mimir — long-term metrics, blocks on Garage S3
VictoriaLogs — logs, 7 day retention
Grafana — the single pane of glass
The other two clusters deploy only egress Services
where these would be.

g.title: o_local->o_store
g.text: remote-write and logs

g.title: o_trick
g.text: Why the other two need no extra configuration
The remote-write and log-sink hostnames are the
SAME STRING in all three clusters. In Ottawa that
name is the real Service. Elsewhere the location
tree ships only an ExternalName Service of exactly
that name pointing at the tailnet FQDN.
So Fluent Bit and Prometheus are configured
identically everywhere. Worth copying.

g.title: o_probe
g.text: Probes check both paths on purpose
Gatus checks the in-cluster endpoint AND its
tailnet equivalent, so a broken overlay is
distinguishable from a broken service.

g.title: o_store->s_garage
g.text: metric blocks

g.title: o_trick->t_egress
g.text: resolved by the
egress ProxyGroup

g.title: k_media
g.text: Media
— Ottawa and Robbinsdale
Plex, the full *arr stack, usenet and two torrent
clients. Libraries on SMB, databases on Ceph.
Ottawa adds the book, manga and audiobook titles.

g.title: k_ai
g.text: Inference
— St. Petersburg
ONE vLLM model spans BOTH DGX Sparks through a
LeaderWorkerSet, and the two halves talk over a
private RDMA rail rather than the LAN.
hermes and cliproxy in Ottawa consume it over the
tailnet, like any other cross-site dependency.

the tailnet
